name: Interglobe Aviation Ltd
about: Interglobe Aviation Ltd (Indigo) is India’s largest passenger airline operating as a low-cost carrier. Serving 86 destinations including 24 international destinations, it provides passengers with a simple, unbundled product, fulfilling its singular brand promise of providing “low fares, on-time flights, and a courteous and hassle-free service” to its customers. IndiGo commenced operations in August 2006 with a single aircraft and has grown its fleet to 262 aircrafts. [1]

business.what: IndiGo (InterGlobe Aviation) is an Indian low-cost airline. It earns money mainly by selling passenger tickets on domestic and international routes, supplemented by ancillary add-on services, its BluChip loyalty programme, and cargo.

ledger.promise: Q4 FY26 capacity (ASK) growth of around 10% YoY
ledger.quote: we are expecting to add capacity of around 10 percent as compared to the same period last year
ledger.actual: Q4 FY26 call: capacity growth for the quarter came in at 3%, below plan. Management blamed the Middle East escalation.

ledger.promise: FY26 CASK ex fuel ex forex up mid-single digit vs FY25
ledger.quote: We are currently estimating mid-single digit percentage increase in our unit costs excluding fuel and forex for the full financial year 2026 as compared to the full financial year 2025
ledger.actual: No full-year FY26 figure given. Q4 FY26 call reports Q4 CASK ex fuel ex forex up about 7% YoY.

ledger.promise: Q1 FY27 capacity growth of around 3-4% YoY
ledger.quote: we are expecting to add capacity of around 3 -4 percent in Q1FY27 as compared to the same period last year
ledger.actual: No ASK figure reported. Q1 FY27 call cites 'measured capacity deployment' and a 'huge amount of cancellation' from the Middle East, which suggests a shortfall.

ledger.promise: Q1 FY27 PRASK up mid-teens YoY
ledger.quote: we currently estimate a mid -teens improvement in unit passenger revenue in Q1FY27 vs Q1FY26
ledger.actual: PRASK not reported. Q1 FY27 revenue was 24,584 vs 20,496 a year earlier, up 20.0%. That fits the guide if capacity growth was small.

ledger.promise: Q2 FY27 flattish capacity and PRASK growth above 25% YoY
ledger.quote: In terms of unit passenger revenue or PRASK for Q2FY27... we are expecting growth of more than 25% compared to the same period last year.
ledger.actual: PRASK and ASK not reported. Q2 FY27 revenue was 23,364 vs 18,555 a year earlier, up 25.9%. That fits flat capacity with PRASK above 25%.

ledger.promise: CASK ex fuel ex forex up mid-to-high single digits in the coming quarters
ledger.quote: we foresee that it's going to be in mid- to high single digits is what our anticipation is right now
ledger.actual: Q1 FY27 call raised it to 'higher side of single digit... early double digits' for FY27. The Q2 FY27 call kept a high-single to early-double-digit range.

ledger.promise: FY27 capacity growth in single digits
ledger.quote: we are holding to the guidance that we gave at the analyst meet. So, it's in single digits.
ledger.actual: Q2 FY27 call narrowed this to 'early single digits' for FY27.

ledger.promise: Bring back all available capacity for the Q3 FY27 peak; decide on damp leases in Q3
ledger.quote: So, we will be bringing back all the capacity that we have.
ledger.actual: Q2 FY27 call guides Q3 capacity to only early single-digit growth, with cuts weighted to international. Damp-leased widebody operations have ended.

ledger.promise: Restore full Middle East capacity by end of June 2026
ledger.quote: we intend to kind of scale back to full capacity by the end of June
ledger.actual: No capacity figure given. The Q1 and Q2 FY27 calls still cite disruption in international corridors and the 'prevailing geopolitical environment' as limits on capacity.

ledger.promise: Pratt & Whitney-related groundings to fall from the 40s to the 30s by end of calendar 2026
ledger.quote: Our Pratt and Whitney-related groundings are currently in the 40s and are expected to trend down wards by the end of the year in the 30's
ledger.actual: Deadline is December 2026. No later call in these materials updates the grounding count.

ledger.promise: Double in size by end of decade; capacity growth back to early double digits after FY27, mid-teens in FY28
ledger.quote: to double in size by the end of the decade.
ledger.actual: Reaffirmed on the Q1 and Q2 FY27 calls. FY27 capacity growth is now early single digits, so FY28-FY30 have to compound faster to get there.

ledger.promise: Prepay USD 450mn (4,340 crore) of finance lease obligations via the GIFT City entity, to fund aircraft and engines
ledger.quote: we are also prepaying some of our finance lease obligations towards our gift city entity aggregating USD 450mn (43.4 bn rupees), such funds will be utilized towards acquisition of aircraft and engines
ledger.actual: Not reported on later calls. Borrowings went from 77,749 (FY26) to 87,303 (FY27 line). FY26 investing outflow was only 1,943.

credibility.label: low
credibility.summary: Every capacity and cost guide that a later call settles has been missed or revised the wrong way: Q4 FY26 capacity came in at 3% against about 10%, FY27 capacity went from single digits to early single digits, the Q3 plan to restore all capacity was dropped, and cost-ex-fuel guidance rose from mid-to-high single digits to early double digits. Management mostly blames outside events (FX, FDTL rules, the Middle East), and the PRASK guides cannot be checked directly, though revenue growth of 20.0% in Q1 FY27 and 25.9% in Q2 FY27 is consistent with them.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Pricing is offsetting higher costs: 'we keep testing high levels of yields in order to offset largely the increased levels of cost'.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20.0% YoY (24,584 vs 20,496), but EBITDA fell from 5,226 to 3,267 and PAT went from 2,176 to -238. Pricing did not offset costs.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Q2 FY27 PRASK up more than 25%, but it 'did not fully offset the abnormally elevated costs', with fuel CASK up 69%.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25.9% to 23,364. EBITDA improved from 580 to 1,907, but PAT was still -1,879 (vs -2,582). TTM PAT is -4,105.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Long-term plan unchanged: double in size by end of decade, with more than 1 aircraft delivery per week.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Investing outflow fell from 12,758 in FY25 to 1,943 in FY26, while borrowings rose from 66,810 (FY25) to 77,749 (FY26) and 87,303 (FY27 line). Growth is being funded with more debt, not cash investing.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Q3 FY26 profit was hit by one-offs: December disruptions (more than 2,500 cancellations) and a 970 crore labour-law provision.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Q3 FY26 EBITDA held at 5,367 (22.9% margin) while PBT was only 562. The gap fits a below-EBITDA exceptional charge of roughly that size.

bull.point: Revenue is growing fast even with little capacity growth, which is consistent with the PRASK guides
bull.evidence: Revenue rose 20.0% YoY in Q1 FY27 and 25.9% in Q2 FY27, against guides of mid-teens PRASK on 3-4% capacity and more than 25% PRASK on flat capacity.
bull.source: reported numbers; Q1 FY27 call p7

bull.point: Pricing strength is guided to last into the seasonally strong Q3
bull.evidence: Q3 FY27 PRASK guided at more than 25% YoY based on October trends, with load factor flat.

bull.point: Cash generation has held up and growth targets are intact
bull.evidence: Cash from operations was 23,470 in FY26 against 24,151 in FY25. FY28 mid-teens capacity growth and the long-term targets were reaffirmed, and the wide-body exit is guided as accretive to spreads.
bull.source: reported numbers; Q2 FY27 call p7, p13

bear.evidence: Q4 FY26 came in at 3% against about 10%. FY27 went from single digits to early single digits, and the plan to bring back all capacity in Q3 FY27 became early single-digit growth.
bear.source: Q4 FY26 call p6; Q2 FY27 call p6

bear.point: Unit costs are rising faster than guided, and losses persist
bear.evidence: CASK ex fuel ex forex guidance went from mid single digits (FY26) to late single to early double digits (FY27). Three of the last four quarters were losses, and TTM PAT is -4,105.
bear.source: Q3 FY26 call p7; Q2 FY27 call p10; reported numbers

bear.point: Leverage is climbing while profits are negative
bear.evidence: Borrowings rose from 51,280 (FY24) to 87,303 (FY27 line), and FY26 PAT was -2,394. Doubling by end of decade needs heavy fleet spending, and OEM delivery delays were flagged.
bear.source: reported numbers; Q2 FY27 call p11, p13
